days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: Present Perfect (ever, never, already, yet, so far) va Past Simple farqi — iş tajribasi haqida gapiriş va motivatsion xat yoziş.

sections.titleUz: Grammatika: Present Perfect va Past Simple
Gapiriş: tajriba, yutuq va orzudagi iş

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: colleague — hamkasb.
exercises.question: What does “colleague” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos zamonni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: “Two years ago” — aniq vaqt: Past Simple (moved).
exercises.question: We ___ to Tashkent two years ago.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni Present Perfect şaklida yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: She + has + V3: has achieved.
exercises.text: This year she ___ (achieve) all her goals.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Inkor oxirida yet: I haven’t received it yet.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I didn’t receive my contract yet already.
I haven’t received my contract yet.
I haven’t received my contract already.
I have received not my contract yet.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Heç … ganmisiz?” = Have you ever …? (tajriba).
exercises.source: Siz heç kafeda işlaganmisiz?
accepted: Have you ever worked in a cafe
Have you ever worked in a café
Have you ever worked at a cafe
Have you ever worked at a café

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ega + has + just + V3: She has just sent her CV.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: promotion — lavozimga kötariliş, skill — könikma, hire — işga olmoq, recently — yaqinda.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: “Yesterday” — aniq vaqt; u bilan Present Perfect işlatilmaydi. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: We can say “I have finished the report yesterday.”

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: must, might, may, could, can’t — taxmin va ehtimol; texnologiya haqida fikr bildiriş va dalil bilan taxmin qiliş.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: reliable — işonçli.
exercises.question: What does “reliable” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos modalni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Aniq emas, faqat ehtimol — might.
exercises.question: Take an umbrella. It ___ rain this afternoon.

exercises.instructionUz: Böş joyga must yoki can’t yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Bir soat oldin ovqatlandi — oç bölişi mumkin emas: can’t.
exercises.text: He had a big lunch an hour ago. He ___ be hungry.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Modal + boşlanğiç fe’l: could be.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: It could to be the router.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Uyda bölsa kerak” — dalil bilan taxmin: must be at home.
exercises.source: Chiroq yoniq. U uyda bölsa kerak.
accepted: The light is on. She must be at home
The light is on. He must be at home
The lights are on. She must be at home
The lights are on. He must be at home

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ega + must + be + V-ing: They must be sleeping.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: replace — örnini egallamoq, device — qurilma, improve — yaxşilamoq, probably — ehtimol.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: “Bölişi mumkin emas” taxmini can’t bilan aytiladi, mustn’t bilan emas. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: “It mustn’t be true” means “It is impossible that it is true”.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: Passive Voice (am / is / are / was / were + V3, by) — tarixiy joylar, sayohat va ekologiya haqida gapiriş, qisqa qöllanma yoziş.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: souvenir — esdalik sovğasi.
exercises.question: What does “souvenir” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Passive şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Köplik ega + ötgan zamon: were taken.
exercises.question: These photos ___ in Termez last summer.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni Present Simple passive şaklida yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Ega birlik — is + V3: is spoken.
exercises.text: Uzbek ___ (speak) by about 35 million people.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Passive inkor: wasn’t + V3.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Qurilgan” — was built; yil oldidan in.
exercises.source: Bu köprik 1965-yilda qurilgan.
accepted: This bridge was built in 1965
The bridge was built in 1965

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ega + are + V3 + by …: Carpets are made by hand.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: waste — çiqindi, reduce — kamaytirmoq, crowded — odam gavjum, local — mahalliy.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Passive’da bajaruvçi köpinça aytilmaydi; by faqat kerak bölganda qöşiladi. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: In a passive sentence we must always say who did the action with “by”.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: used to / didn’t use to / would — ötmişdagi odatlar va holatlar; ilgari va hozirni soliştiriş.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: neighbour — qöşni.
exercises.question: What does “neighbour” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Ilgarigi holat: There used to be …
exercises.question: There ___ a park here, but now it’s a car park.

exercises.instructionUz: Böş joyni inkor şaklda töldiring.
exercises.explanationUz: Inkor: didn’t use to + fe’l.
exercises.text: She ___ (not / like) spicy food, but now she loves it.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Holat fe’li (live) bilan would emas, used to: We used to live in Nukus.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: We used to live in Nukus.
We use to live in Nukus.
We were used to live in Nukus.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Ilgari … çekardi” — used to smoke.
exercises.source: Otam ilgari çekardi.
accepted: My father used to smoke
My dad used to smoke

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan söroq gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: Did + ega + use to + fe’l: Did you use to wear glasses?

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: habit — odat, tradition — an’ana, childhood — bolalik, nowadays — hozirgi kunda.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Used to faqat ötmiş uçun. Hozirgi odat — Present Simple. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: We can say “I use to drink tea every morning” about the present.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: First Conditional (if + Present, will), when / as soon as / until / unless — retsept, maslahat va oqibat haqida gapiriş.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: ingredient — masalliq.
exercises.question: What does “ingredient” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Natija bölagi — will + fe’l.
exercises.question: If you don’t wash the rice, the plov ___ sticky.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni töğri şaklda yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: When bölagida Present Simple; everyone birlik hisoblanadi: arrives.
exercises.text: We will start eating when everyone ___ (arrive).

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Unless’ning özi inkor: Unless you hurry …
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Unless you don’t hurry, we’ll be late.
Unless you hurry, we’ll be late.
Unless you will hurry, we’ll be late.
Unless you hurry, we are late tomorrow.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “… bilanoq” = as soon as; bölakda Present Simple.
exercises.source: Suv qaynaşi bilanoq guruçni soling.
accepted: Add the rice as soon as the water boils
Put the rice in as soon as the water boils
As soon as the water boils, add the rice
As soon as the water boils add the rice
Put in the rice as soon as the water boils

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: If + Present Simple, … will …: If it rains we will stay home.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: boil — qaynatmoq, fry — qovurmoq, fresh — sarxil, avoid — saqlanmoq.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: If bölagida kelajak ma’nosida ham Present Simple keladi — fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: In “If it rains tomorrow, …” we use the Present Simple, not “will”.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: Present Perfect Continuous, for / since, How long …? va Present Perfect bilan farqi — iş jarayoni haqida gapiriş va hisobot xati.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: deadline — oxirgi muddat.
exercises.question: What does “deadline” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Davom etayotgan jarayon + for: have been waiting.
exercises.question: We ___ for the doctor for an hour.

exercises.instructionUz: For yoki since ni yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Monday — boşlaniş nuqtasi: since.
exercises.text: It has been raining ___ Monday.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Miqdor (four emails) — natija: Present Perfect Simple.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I have been sending four emails today.
I have sent four emails today.
I am sending four emails today already.
I have been sent four emails today.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “… dan beri yaşayapsiz” — How long have you been living …?
exercises.source: Toşkentda qançadan beri yaşayapsiz?
accepted: How long have you been living in Tashkent
How long have you lived in Tashkent

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ega + has been + V-ing + for …: She has been working remotely for a year.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: client — mijoz, commute — işga qatnamoq, earn — pul topmoq, lonely — yolğiz.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Know, like, want kabi holat fe’llari continuous’da işlatilmaydi — fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: We don’t usually use “know” in the Present Perfect Continuous.

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: Second Conditional (if + Past Simple, would), If I were you — xayoliy vaziyatlar, maslahat va esse.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: heritage — meros.
exercises.question: What does “heritage” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Xayoliy şart natijasi — would + fe’l.
exercises.question: If I spoke Korean, I ___ in Seoul.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni töğri şaklda yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: If bölagi — Past Simple: had.
exercises.text: If we ___ (have) a garden, we would grow our own vegetables.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: If bölagida would işlatilmaydi.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: If I would be rich, I would help everyone.
If I was rich, I will help everyone.
If I were rich, I would help everyone.
If I am rich, I would help everyone.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Men sizning örningizda bölsam” = If I were you.
exercises.source: Men sizning örningizda bölsam, bu gilamni sotmasdim.
accepted: If I were you, I wouldn’t sell this carpet
If I were you, I wouldn't sell this carpet
If I were you, I would not sell this carpet
If I were you I wouldn’t sell this carpet

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ega + would + fe’l + if + Past Simple.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: preserve — asramoq, generation — avlod, craft — hunar, proud of — faxrlanmoq.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Second Conditional’dagi Past Simple ötgan vaqtni emas, xayoliylikni bildiradi. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: In “If I had a car, I would drive to work”, the speaker had a car in the past.

vocab.explanationEn: Knowledge or skill that you get from doing a job or activity.
vocab.exampleEn: She has five years of experience in marketing.
vocab.exampleUz: Uning marketingda beş yillik tajribasi bor.

vocab.explanationEn: The series of jobs that you do during your working life.
vocab.exampleEn: He started his career as a waiter in a small café.
vocab.exampleUz: U kasb yölini kiçkina kafeda ofitsiant bölib boşlagan.

vocab.explanationEn: To ask officially for a job or a place, usually in writing.
vocab.exampleEn: I have applied for a job at the bank.

vocab.explanationEn: A meeting where someone asks you questions to see if you are right for a job.
vocab.exampleEn: My interview is on Monday at ten.

vocab.explanationEn: To give someone a job.
vocab.exampleEn: The company hired three new engineers last month.
vocab.exampleUz: Kompaniya ötgan oy uçta yangi muhandisni işga oldi.

vocab.explanationEn: A person that you work with.
vocab.exampleEn: My colleagues helped me a lot in my first week.
vocab.exampleUz: Birinçi haftamda hamkasblarim menga köp yordam berişdi.

vocab.explanationEn: A move to a more important job in the same company.
vocab.exampleEn: Dilshod got a promotion after two years.
vocab.exampleUz: Dilşod ikki yildan keyin lavozimga kötarildi.

vocab.explanationEn: To succeed in doing something after working hard.
vocab.exampleEn: Our team has achieved a lot this year.
vocab.exampleUz: Jamoamiz bu yil köp narsaga erişdi.

vocab.explanationEn: An ability to do something well because you have practised it.
vocab.exampleEn: Good communication is an important skill.

vocab.explanationEn: Having the job of looking after something or someone.
vocab.exampleEn: I am responsible for the company website.

vocab.explanationEn: Not long ago.
vocab.exampleEn: I have recently started a new job.

vocab.explanationEn: Until now.
vocab.exampleEn: So far I have visited three clients today.

vocab.explanationEn: A machine or tool made for a special purpose, for example a phone.
vocab.exampleEn: Turn off all devices before the exam.

vocab.explanationEn: A machine that can do work automatically, often instead of a person.
vocab.exampleEn: A robot cleans the floor in our office at night.

vocab.explanationEn: To take the place of someone or something.
vocab.exampleEn: Machines might replace some cashiers in supermarkets.
vocab.exampleUz: Maşinalar supermarketlardagi ayrim kassirlarning örnini egallaşi mumkin.

vocab.explanationEn: Working by itself, without a person controlling it.
vocab.exampleEn: The doors are automatic — they open when you come close.

vocab.explanationEn: A program that you use on a phone or computer.
vocab.exampleEn: I pay my bills with a banking app.

vocab.explanationEn: Facts and numbers that are collected and used, often by computers.
vocab.exampleEn: The app collects data about your sleep.

vocab.explanationEn: Something that you can trust to work well.
vocab.exampleEn: This old laptop is still very reliable.
vocab.exampleUz: Bu eski noutbuk hali ham juda işonçli.

vocab.explanationEn: To make something better, or to become better.
vocab.exampleEn: New software has improved our work.

vocab.explanationEn: In place of someone or something.
vocab.exampleEn: Many people use apps instead of cash.
vocab.exampleUz: Köp odamlar naqd pul örniga ilovalardan foydalanadi.

vocab.explanationEn: Almost certainly; very likely.
vocab.exampleEn: It will probably rain tomorrow.

vocab.explanationEn: Able to happen or be done.
vocab.exampleEn: Is it possible to fix my phone today?

vocab.explanationEn: The part that gives power to a phone, car or other device.
vocab.exampleEn: My phone battery lasts all day.

vocab.explanationEn: A person who travels to a place for pleasure.
vocab.exampleEn: Thousands of tourists visit Khiva every spring.
vocab.exampleUz: Har bahor Xivaga minglab sayyohlar keladi.

vocab.explanationEn: Damage to air, water or land caused by harmful substances.
vocab.exampleEn: Air pollution is a big problem in winter.

vocab.explanationEn: Things that are thrown away because they are not needed.
vocab.exampleEn: Plastic waste is collected every Tuesday.

vocab.explanationEn: To treat used things so that they can be used again.
vocab.exampleEn: Glass bottles can be recycled many times.
vocab.exampleUz: Şişa idişlarni köp marta qayta işlaş mumkin.

vocab.explanationEn: To keep someone or something safe from harm.
vocab.exampleEn: Old buildings must be protected.

vocab.explanationEn: To cause harm to something.
vocab.exampleEn: The wall was damaged by heavy rain.

vocab.explanationEn: A person whose job is to show a place to tourists.
vocab.exampleEn: Our guide told us the history of the mosque.
vocab.exampleUz: Gidimiz bizga masjid tarixini aytib berdi.

vocab.explanationEn: Something you buy to remember a place you visited.
vocab.exampleEn: I bought a small ceramic plate as a souvenir.
vocab.exampleUz: Esdalik uçun kiçkina sopol likopça sotib oldim.

vocab.explanationEn: To make a building or structure; past forms: built, built.
vocab.exampleEn: The madrasah was built in the 15th century.

vocab.explanationEn: Full of people.
vocab.exampleEn: The old city is very crowded in May.
vocab.exampleUz: May oyida eski şahar juda gavjum böladi.

vocab.explanationEn: To make something smaller in size or amount.
vocab.exampleEn: We can reduce waste by using our own bags.
vocab.exampleUz: Öz sumkalarimizni işlatib, çiqindini kamaytira olamiz.

vocab.explanationEn: Belonging to the area where you are.
vocab.exampleEn: Try the local bread — it is delicious.
vocab.exampleUz: Mahalliy nonni tatib köring — juda mazali.

vocab.explanationEn: Something that you do often and regularly, sometimes without thinking.
vocab.exampleEn: Reading before bed is a good habit.
vocab.exampleUz: Uxlaşdan oldin kitob öqiş — yaxşi odat.

vocab.explanationEn: The time when you are a child.
vocab.exampleEn: I spent my childhood in a village near Fergana.

vocab.explanationEn: A person who lives near you.
vocab.exampleEn: Our neighbours used to bring us fresh bread.
vocab.exampleUz: Qöşnilarimiz bizga yangi non olib kelişardi.

vocab.explanationEn: To come together in one place.
vocab.exampleEn: The family gathered at grandma’s house every Friday.
vocab.exampleUz: Oila har juma buvimning uyiga yiğilardi.

vocab.explanationEn: At the present time, compared with the past.
vocab.exampleEn: Nowadays most people pay by card.
vocab.exampleUz: Hozirgi kunda köpçilik karta orqali tölaydi.

vocab.explanationEn: To stop doing something that you did regularly.
vocab.exampleEn: My father gave up smoking ten years ago.
vocab.exampleUz: Otam çekişni ön yil oldin taşlagan.

vocab.explanationEn: The usual order in which you do things every day.
vocab.exampleEn: A morning routine helps me start the day well.
vocab.exampleUz: Ertalabki tartib kunni yaxşi boşlaşga yordam beradi.

vocab.explanationEn: A custom that people have followed for a long time.
vocab.exampleEn: Cooking sumalak in spring is an old tradition.

vocab.explanationEn: To become different.
vocab.exampleEn: Our street has changed a lot since I was a child.

vocab.explanationEn: Good for your body, or not ill.
vocab.exampleEn: I try to eat healthy food.

vocab.explanationEn: To use time doing something or being somewhere.
vocab.exampleEn: We used to spend our summers at the lake.

vocab.explanationEn: Used in negative sentences to say that something has stopped.
vocab.exampleEn: I don’t play computer games any more.

vocab.explanationEn: One of the foods that you use to make a dish.
vocab.exampleEn: Plov has simple ingredients: rice, carrots, meat and oil.
vocab.exampleUz: Palovning masalliqlari oddiy: guruç, sabzi, göşt va yoğ.

vocab.explanationEn: A set of instructions for cooking a dish.
vocab.exampleEn: This recipe is from my grandmother.

vocab.explanationEn: To heat water or food until it bubbles.
vocab.exampleEn: Boil the potatoes for twenty minutes.

vocab.explanationEn: To cook food in hot oil.
vocab.exampleEn: First fry the onions until they are golden.

vocab.explanationEn: To be damaged by too much heat.
vocab.exampleEn: If you leave the rice too long, it will burn.
vocab.exampleUz: Guruçni juda uzoq qoldirsangiz, u kuyib qoladi.

vocab.explanationEn: The food that you usually eat, or a special plan for eating.
vocab.exampleEn: A good diet includes fruit and vegetables.
vocab.exampleUz: Yaxşi ovqatlaniş tartibida meva va sabzavotlar bor.

vocab.explanationEn: The amount of food for one person.
vocab.exampleEn: The portions in this café are very big.

vocab.explanationEn: The flavour of food; to try food to see what it is like.
vocab.exampleEn: Taste the soup before you add salt.
vocab.exampleUz: Tuz solişdan oldin şörvani tatib köring.

vocab.explanationEn: Recently made, picked or bought; not old.
vocab.exampleEn: We buy fresh vegetables at the bazaar.

vocab.explanationEn: To try not to do or eat something.
vocab.exampleEn: My doctor told me to avoid sugar.

vocab.explanationEn: Except if; if not.
vocab.exampleEn: You won’t lose weight unless you change your diet.

vocab.explanationEn: Immediately after something happens.
vocab.exampleEn: I’ll call you as soon as the plov is ready.
vocab.exampleUz: Palov tayyor bölişi bilanoq sizga qöngiroq qilaman.

vocab.explanationEn: Work that you do from home or another place, not in the office.
vocab.exampleEn: Remote work saves me two hours a day.
vocab.exampleUz: Masofaviy iş menga kuniga ikki soat vaqt tejaydi.

vocab.explanationEn: A person who works for different clients, not for one company.
vocab.exampleEn: As a freelancer, she chooses her own projects.
vocab.exampleUz: Frilanser sifatida u loyihalarni özi tanlaydi.

vocab.explanationEn: The time or date by which you must finish something.
vocab.exampleEn: The deadline for the report is Friday.

vocab.explanationEn: A person or company that pays for a service.
vocab.exampleEn: I have been working with this client since March.
vocab.exampleUz: Bu mijoz bilan martdan beri işlayapman.

vocab.explanationEn: A meeting that happens on the internet, by video.

explanationUz: Present Perfect (have / has + fe’lning 3-şakli) ötgan voqeani HOZIRGI natija yoki tajriba sifatida aytadi, vaqti esa muhim emas: I have worked in two banks (hayotimdagi tajriba). Past Simple esa ANIQ, tugagan vaqtdagi voqea: I worked at Kapitalbank in 2021.

Aniq vaqt körsatilsa (yesterday, last year, in 2020, two weeks ago, when I was a student) faqat Past Simple işlatiladi. “I have finished university in 2022” — xato; töğrisi: I finished university in 2022.

Present Perfect bilan köp uçraydigan sözlar: ever, never, already, yet, just, recently, so far, this week / this year (hali tugamagan davr). Have you ever worked abroad? I have just sent my CV. She hasn’t found a job yet.
Suhbatda odatda Present Perfect bilan boşlanadi, tafsilotga ötilganda Past Simple keladi: “Have you ever had an interview in English?” — “Yes, I have. I had one last month. It went well.”

grammar.titleUz: Taxmin modallari: must, might, could, can’t
explanationUz: Modal fe’llar orqali biror narsaga qançalik işonçimiz komilligini körsatamiz. Must — deyarli aniq (dalil bor): The screen is black — the battery must be empty. Can’t — deyarli aniq EMAS: He can’t be at work — his car is at home.

Might, may va could — “bölişi mumkin, aniq emas”: The parcel might arrive today. Robots may replace some jobs. It could be a problem with the app. Uçalasi ham taxminan bir xil ma’noda, may biroz rasmiyroq.

Modaldan keyin fe’l doim boşlanğiç şaklda keladi, to işlatilmaydi va -s qöşilmaydi: She might be busy (she mights / might to be — xato). Hozirgi davom etayotgan iş uçun: must / might + be + -ing: He must be sleeping.
Must not’ni taxmin uçun işlatmaymiz: “Bu töğri bölişi mumkin emas” = It can’t be true (It mustn’t be true — xato). Mustn’t taqiq ma’nosida: You mustn’t use your phone here.

grammar.titleUz: Passive Voice: Present va Past Simple
explanationUz: Passive (majhul nisbat) — harakatni KIM qilgani emas, NIMAGA qilingani muhim bölganda işlatiladi: The mosque was built in 1420. (Kim qurgani muhim emas yoki noma’lum.) Özbekçadagi “qurilgan, töplanadi, işlab çiqariladi” şakllariga öxşaydi.

Yasaliş: be + fe’lning 3-şakli (V3). Present Simple: am / is / are + V3 — Paper is recycled here. Past Simple: was / were + V3 — The bridge was damaged by the flood. Be şakli egaga moslaşadi: The bottle is …, The bottles are …

Harakatni bajaruvçini aytiş kerak bölsa by işlatiladi: The museum was opened by the president. Lekin köp hollarda bajaruvçi aytilmaydi, çunki u aniq emas yoki muhim emas: My bag was stolen (kim ögirlagani noma’lum).

Inkor va söroq be orqali yasaladi: Plastic isn’t recycled in our street. Was the hotel built recently? When was the city founded? Köp uçraydigan xato — be ni taşlab ketiş: “The palace built in 1800” örniga The palace was built in 1800.

grammar.titleUz: Used to va would: ötmişdagi odatlar
grammar.titleEn: Used to and would for past habits
explanationUz: Used to + fe’l — ilgari muntazam bölgan, endi esa yöq odat yoki holat: I used to walk to school (endi yurmayman). Özbekçada “… ardim / … ar edim” şakliga mos keladi: “maktabga piyoda borardim”.
Inkor va söroqda did işlatiladi, used esa use ga aylanadi: I didn’t use to like vegetables. Did you use to play outside? (“Did you used to” — xato, çunki did bilan fe’l boşlanğiç şaklda.)

Would ham ötmişdagi takrorlanadigan HARAKATlarni aytadi, köpinça hikoyada: Every Friday my grandmother would bake bread. Lekin would HOLAT fe’llari bilan (be, have, live, like, know) işlatilmaydi: I used to have a cat (I would have a cat — bu ma’noda xato).
Bir marta bölgan voqea uçun used to ham, would ham işlatilmaydi — oddiy Past Simple kerak: In 2015 we moved to Tashkent. Hozirgi odatni Present Simple bilan aytamiz, “I use to” deb aytilmaydi.

grammar.titleEn: First conditional and future time clauses
explanationUz: First Conditional — kelajakda REAL, ehtimoli katta şart va uning natijasi: If you add too much salt, nobody will eat it. Tuzilma: if + Present Simple, … will + fe’l. Özbekçadagi “agar … sa, … adi” şakliga mos.

MUHIM: if bölagida will işlatilmaydi, kelajak ma’nosi bölsa ham Present Simple keladi: If it rains tomorrow, we will cook at home. (“If it will rain” — xato.) Natija bölagida will dan taşqari may / might / can ham keliş mumkin: If we leave now, we might catch the bus.
Xuddi şu qoida vaqt boğlovçilariga ham tegişli: when, as soon as, before, after, until. I will call you when I get home. As soon as the water boils, add the pasta. Bu bölaklarda ham will yöq.
Unless = if … not (“agar … masa”): Unless you stir it, the rice will stick = If you don’t stir it, the rice will stick. Unless bilan inkor ikki marta işlatilmaydi: “Unless you don’t hurry” — xato.

For — davomiylik (for two hours, for six months), since — boşlaniş nuqtasi (since 2023, since Monday, since I was a student). How long …? savoli bilan köp keladi: How long have you been learning English?
Bu zamon yaqinda tugagan, lekin izi körinib turgan iş uçun ham işlatiladi: Your eyes are red. Have you been crying? — I’m tired because I have been writing reports all day.

Natija va miqdor uçun oddiy Present Perfect kerak: I have written three reports (neçta — natija). I have been writing reports (jarayon). Holat fe’llari (know, like, want, have — egalik) continuous’da işlatilmaydi: I have known him for years (I have been knowing — xato).

reading.title: From Waitress to Web Developer
paragraphs: Nodira is twenty-eight and works as a web developer in Tashkent. Her career did not start with computers. After school she worked as a waitress in her uncle’s café for three years. She enjoyed talking to customers, but she wanted a job with more chances to grow.

In 2020 she started an online programming course in the evenings. It was hard to study after long shifts, and twice she almost gave up. Her friend Bobur, who was already a programmer, helped her with difficult tasks. In 2022 she applied for a junior position at a small IT company and they hired her after two interviews.

Since then Nodira has worked on more than twenty websites. She has learned to work in a team and she is now responsible for training new developers. Last month she got her first promotion. “I have made a lot of mistakes,” she says, “but every mistake has taught me something. The skills I learned in the café still help me: I listen to clients carefully.”

reading.title: Will a Robot Take My Job?
paragraphs: Last year a large supermarket in Tashkent installed self-checkout machines. Now customers can scan and pay for their shopping without a cashier. Some shoppers love it because it is fast. Others prefer to talk to a real person, especially older customers who find the machines confusing.

Lola has worked at the supermarket for six years. When the machines arrived, she was worried. “I thought they might replace me,” she says. But the company did not fire anyone. Instead, it trained the cashiers to help customers with the new machines and to work in online orders. Lola now prepares shopping for home delivery and says her job is more interesting.

Experts say that automation will probably change many jobs rather than destroy them. Machines are reliable at simple, repeated tasks, but they can’t understand people as well as humans can. Jobs that need care, creativity and communication may become even more important. Still, workers will need to learn new skills, and this could be difficult for some of them.

paragraphs: Khiva is one of the oldest cities in Central Asia. Its inner town, Itchan Kala, was built behind high clay walls, and today more than fifty historic buildings are protected there. Every year the city is visited by thousands of tourists from all over the world, and the number grows each spring.

More visitors bring money to local families, but they also create problems. A few years ago the streets were full of plastic bottles, and some old walls were damaged by people who climbed them to take photos. In summer the narrow streets became so crowded that local people avoided the centre.

Now the town has a plan to reduce these problems. Bottles are collected in special bins and taken to a recycling centre in Urgench. Free drinking water is offered at several points, so visitors can refill their bottles. Tour groups are limited to twenty people, and guides are trained to explain why the walls must not be climbed. Small hotels that use solar energy are given a “green” sign by the city.

reading.title: Our Mahalla, Then and Now
paragraphs: Mavluda opa is sixty-five and has lived in the same mahalla in Namangan all her life. “When I was a girl, everybody used to know everybody,” she remembers. “There were no phones in most houses, so if you needed something, you would simply knock on your neighbour’s door.”

In the evenings the children would play in the street until it got dark, and their parents would sit on wooden benches and talk. On Fridays the women used to bake bread together in a big clay oven, and the smell filled the whole street. “We didn’t use to have much money,” she says, “but we never felt poor.”

Nowadays life is different. Most families have cars, and the old oven was replaced by a small bakery. Children spend more time with phones than outside. Still, some traditions have not changed. When there is a wedding or a funeral, the whole mahalla gathers to help, just as it used to. And every spring Mavluda opa’s grandchildren help her cook sumalak for the neighbours.

reading.title: Kitchen Rules from a Plov Master
paragraphs: Oybek has cooked plov for weddings in Andijan for twenty years. Every Sunday he teaches a free class for young people in his mahalla. “Plov is not difficult,” he says, “but it has strict rules. If you break them, you will get rice porridge, not plov.”

His first rule is about the oil. If the oil isn’t hot enough, the meat will not get a brown colour. His second rule is patience: once the rice is in the kazan, you must not stir it. “As soon as you stir the rice, it will break and become sticky,” he explains. He also tells his students to wash the rice at least five times, until the water is clear.

Oybek believes that good food is also healthy food. He uses less oil than his teacher did and adds more carrots and chickpeas. “People think plov is unhealthy,” he laughs, “but if you eat a normal portion with a fresh salad, it won’t hurt you. The problem starts when you eat three plates.”

reading.title: Working from the Kitchen Table
paragraphs: For the last two years, Javlon has been working as a freelance designer from his flat in Samarkand. His clients are in Germany, Turkey and Kazakhstan. He has never met most of them in person — they talk in online meetings and send messages.

At first remote work felt like a dream. He didn’t have to commute for an hour, and he could choose his own hours. But lately things have been changing. “I have been working longer than ever,” he admits. “My laptop is always on the kitchen table, so I check emails at midnight. My wife says I have been ignoring the family.” He has also been feeling lonely, because he hardly talks to other designers.

So this month Javlon has been trying a new routine. He stops work at seven, and he has rented a desk in a co-working space two days a week. “It costs money, but I have been sleeping better and I have met three other freelancers,” he says. “Remote work is great, but you need rules. Otherwise the job will take over your whole life.”

reading.title: The Last Potter in the Family?
paragraphs: In the small town of Rishtan, Alisher Nazirov makes the famous blue ceramics that his family has made for six generations. His plates and bowls are sold in Tashkent and even in Europe. But Alisher is worried. His two sons work in Russia and say they will not come back to the workshop. “If they came home,” he says, “I would teach them everything I know. But they earn more money there.”

Many traditional crafts in Central Asia face the same problem. Learning to make ceramics, carpets or silk takes years, and young people often want faster ways to earn a living. Some experts believe that if crafts were taught in ordinary schools, more children would become interested. Others say that the problem is money: if artists earned more, young people would stay.

There is some good news. Last year Alisher started teaching free classes to local teenagers on Saturdays. Eight students come regularly, and two of them have already sold their first bowls online. “If you had asked me ten years ago, I would have said that pottery would die,” Alisher laughs. “Now I think it has a future — if we pass it on.”

Doctor: Tell me about your diet. What do you usually have for breakfast?

writing.promptEn: You have seen a job advert for an assistant at an international hotel in Samarkand. Write a short cover letter. Say what experience you have, what you have achieved and why you want this job.
writing.instructionUz: Samarqanddagi xalqaro mehmonxonada yordamçi lavozimi uçun qisqa motivatsion xat yozing: qanday tajribangiz bor, nimalarga erişgansiz va nega aynan şu işni xohlaysiz. Present Perfect’ni kamida uç marta va aniq vaqt bilan Past Simple’ni kamida bir marta işlating.
checklistUz: Rasmiy murojaat (Dear Sir or Madam,) va yakun (Yours faithfully,) bor.
Qaysi lavozimga ariza berayotganingiz birinçi gapda aytilgan.
Tajriba Present Perfect bilan (I have worked …), aniq sana Past Simple bilan berilgan.
Kamida bitta yutuq aniq misol bilan körsatilgan.
Nega bu işni xohlaşingiz va qaçon suhbatga kela olişingiz yozilgan.

mustInclude.whyUz: Xatning asosiy mavzusi — tajribangiz; “experience” sözi kerak.
Tajribani Present Perfect bilan bering: “I have worked / I have learned …”.
Qaysi lavozimga ariza berayotganingizni ayting: “I am writing to apply for …”.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to apply for the position of assistant at your hotel. I have worked at a guest house in Bukhara for two years, where I am responsible for bookings and for welcoming guests. In that time I have learned to solve problems quickly and stay polite with every visitor. Last year I created a simple guide to the city in English, and our online reviews improved. I have also completed a course in hotel management. I would like to work for your hotel because I want to grow in an international team and use my English every day. I am available for an interview at any time. Yours faithfully, Kamola Rahimova

writing.promptEn: Your English teacher has asked you to write a short opinion paragraph: “Robots and computers will do most jobs in 20 years.” Do you agree? Give your opinion and two reasons with examples.
writing.instructionUz: “20 yildan keyin işlarning köpini robot va kompyuterlar bajaradi” degan fikr haqida qisqa xulosa-paragraf yozing. Rozimisiz? Fikringiz va ikkita sababni misol bilan keltiring. Kamida uçta taxmin modalini (might, could, can’t, must, probably) işlating.
checklistUz: Birinçi gapda fikringiz aniq aytilgan (I partly agree / I don’t agree …).
Ikkita sabab alohida berilgan (Firstly, … Secondly, …).
Har sababga hayotdan misol bor (bank, bozor, şifoxona, maktab).
Kamida uçta taxmin modali işlatilgan.
Oxirida qisqa xulosa (In conclusion, …).

mustInclude.whyUz: Kelajak haqida taxmin — “might” bilan kamida bir gap yozing.
Sabablarni tartib bilan bering: “Firstly, … Secondly, …”.
Paragrafni xulosa bilan yakunlang: “In conclusion, …”.

writing.modelAnswerEn: I partly agree with this statement. Firstly, machines are already doing many simple jobs. In my local supermarket, self-checkout machines have replaced two cashiers, and in twenty years robots might also clean streets and drive taxis. Secondly, computers are becoming cheaper and more reliable, so companies will probably use them more. However, I don’t think robots can do every job. A robot can’t comfort a sick child or teach a teenager who has lost motivation. Doctors, teachers and social workers must understand people, and machines are not good at that. In conclusion, technology could change most jobs, but people will still be needed where care and communication are important.

writing.promptEn: Write a short guide to one interesting place in your town or region for foreign visitors. When was it built or founded? What is it known for? What is made, sold or served there? Give one tip for responsible tourists.
writing.instructionUz: Şahringiz yoki viloyatingizdagi bitta qiziqarli joy haqida xorijlik mehmonlar uçun qisqa qöllanma yozing: qaçon qurilgan, nimasi bilan maşhur, u yerda nima yasaladi yoki sotiladi. Mas’uliyatli sayyohlarga bitta maslahat bering. Kamida törtta passive şakl işlating.
checklistUz: Joyning nomi va qayerdaligi birinçi gapda aytilgan.
Tarix passive bilan berilgan (It was built / founded …).
Hozirgi holat Present passive bilan (… is made / sold / served there).
Mas’uliyatli sayyohlarga bitta aniq maslahat bor.
Kamida törtta passive şakl işlatilgan.

mustInclude.whyUz: Joy tarixini passive bilan bering: “It was built in …”.
U yerda nima sotilişini passive bilan ayting: “… is / are sold there”.
Sayyohlarga maslahatni muloyim qilib bering: “Please …”.

writing.modelAnswerEn: If you visit Kokand, don’t miss the Palace of Khudayar Khan. It was built in the 1870s and it was decorated with beautiful coloured tiles. Today the palace is used as a museum, and old clothes, weapons and jewellery are shown in its rooms. Traditional bread and sweets are sold near the entrance, and green tea is served in a small teahouse in the garden. The palace is visited by many school groups, so it is quieter in the late afternoon. Please don’t touch the painted walls: some of them were damaged in the past and are still being repaired. Bring your own bottle — free water is offered at the gate.

writing.promptEn: Write about how your life has changed since you were a child. What did you use to do that you don’t do any more? What did your family use to do together? What is different now?
writing.instructionUz: Bolaligingizdan beri hayotingiz qanday özgargani haqida yozing: ilgari nima qilardingiz, endi qilmaysiz; oilangiz birga nima qilardi; hozir nima boşqaça. «Used to» iborasini kamida uç marta, «would» va «didn’t use to» iboralarini bir martadan işlating.
checklistUz: Ilgari (When I was a child …) va hozir (Nowadays …) aniq ajratilgan.
Used to kamida uç marta işlatilgan.
Bitta takrorlanadigan harakat would bilan berilgan.
Bitta inkor: I didn’t use to …
Oxirida özgariş haqida fikringiz bor (I miss … / I’m glad …).

mustInclude.whyUz: Mavzu — ötmişdagi odatlar; “used to” albatta kerak.
Takrorlanadigan harakat uçun bitta “would” gap yozing.
Hozirgi holatni “Nowadays …” bilan boşlang.

writing.modelAnswerEn: When I was a child, we used to live in a village near Jizzakh. I used to wake up early because our cow needed water, and after school I would run to the river with my cousins. We didn’t use to have the internet, so in the evenings my grandfather would tell us long stories about his army days. My family used to eat together every evening on the big wooden tapchan in the yard. Nowadays I live in Tashkent and study at university. I see my family only at weekends, and we often eat while looking at our phones. I’m glad that I can study in a big city, but I really miss those quiet evenings in the yard.

writing.promptEn: Your English-speaking friend wants to cook an Uzbek dish for the first time. Write a message with the recipe and three pieces of advice. Explain what will happen if they make a common mistake.
writing.instructionUz: Ingliz tilida gaplaşadigan döstingiz birinçi marta özbek taomini pişirmoqçi. Unga retsept va uçta maslahat yozing: keng tarqalgan xatoga yöl qöysa nima böladi. First Conditional’ni kamida uç marta, when / as soon as / unless dan birini kamida bir marta işlating.
checklistUz: Taom nomi va masalliqlar röyxati bor.
Bosqiçlar tartib bilan berilgan (First, … Then, … Finally, …).
Kamida uçta “If …, … will …” gap bor.
When, as soon as yoki unless kamida bir marta işlatilgan.
Samimiy yakun (Good luck! Send me a photo!).

mustInclude.whyUz: Maslahat First Conditional bilan beriladi: “If you …, it will …”.
Natijani will bilan ayting.
Bosqiçlarni tartib bilan bering: “First, … Then, …”.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Hi Emma! Here is my mum’s recipe for mastava, a rice soup. You need meat, onions, carrots, potatoes, tomatoes and a cup of rice. First, fry the meat and onions in a deep pot. If the oil isn’t hot, the meat won’t get a nice colour. Then add the vegetables and water. As soon as the water boils, put in the rice. Don’t add too much rice — if you do, the soup will become very thick. Cook it for about thirty minutes and taste it before you add salt. Unless you serve it with fresh herbs and a spoon of yoghurt, it won’t taste like real mastava! Good luck, and send me a photo when it is ready. Love, Dilnoza

writing.promptEn: You are working on a project with an international team. Write an email to your manager: explain what you have been doing this week, what you have finished, and one problem you have been having. Ask for help.
writing.instructionUz: Xalqaro jamoada loyiha ustida işlayapsiz. Rahbaringizga xat yozing: bu hafta nima bilan band bölganingiz, nimani tugatganingiz va qanday muammo bölayotganini tuşuntiring, yordam sörang. Present Perfect Continuous’ni kamida ikki marta va oddiy Present Perfect’ni kamida ikki marta işlating.
checklistUz: Neytral-rasmiy murojaat (Hi Mr …, / Dear …,) va yakun (Best regards,).
Jarayon Present Perfect Continuous bilan (I have been working on …).
Tugagan natija Present Perfect bilan (I have finished …).
Bitta muammo va uning sababi aniq yozilgan.
Aniq iltimos bilan yakunlangan (Could you …?).

mustInclude.whyUz: Davom etayotgan iş uçun “have been + -ing” kerak.
Yordamni muloyim sörang: “Could you …?”.
Iş xatini “Best regards,” bilan yakunlang.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Hi Mr Rakhimov, I’m writing with an update on the hotel booking app. This week I have been working on the payment page, and I have finished the design for the mobile version. I have also tested it with five users. However, I have been having problems with the bank’s system: the test payments have been failing since Tuesday, and their support team hasn’t answered my emails. Could you contact them, or give me the phone number of someone there? I don’t want us to miss the deadline next Friday. Thank you for your help. Best regards, Nigora

writing.promptEn: “Young people don’t care about traditions any more.” Write a short essay. Do you agree? What would happen if traditions disappeared? What would you do to keep them alive?
writing.instructionUz: “Yoşlar endi an’analarga qiziqmaydi” degan fikr haqida qisqa esse yozing: rozimisiz, an’analar yöqolsa nima bölardi va ularni asraş uçun siz nima qilgan bölardingiz. Second Conditional’ni kamida uç marta işlating.
checklistUz: Kirişda fikringiz aniq aytilgan.
Ikki-uç paragraf: sabablar va misollar (bayramlar, hunar, taomlar, musiqa).
Kamida uçta “If …, … would …” gap bor.
Bitta aniq taklif: “If I were …, I would …”.
Xulosa paragrafi (To sum up, …).

mustInclude.whyUz: Xayoliy natija — “would + fe’l” kerak.
Taklifingizni “If I were …, I would …” bilan bering.
Esseni xulosa bilan yakunlang: “To sum up, …”.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Many people say that young people don’t care about traditions, but I only partly agree. It is true that teenagers spend a lot of time online, and fewer of them learn crafts like embroidery or pottery. However, most young people still celebrate Navruz and love traditional food. If traditions disappeared, we would lose an important part of who we are. Our holidays would look the same as in any other country, and old skills would die with our grandparents. In my opinion, traditions survive when they are connected to modern life. If I were a teacher, I would ask students to interview their grandparents and make short videos about family customs. If schools did this, young people would feel proud of their culture. To sum up, young people do care about traditions, but they need new ways to discover them.

followUpsEn: Why did you start?
What has been the hardest part?

speaking.questionEn: Describe a tradition in your family or region. What would happen if people stopped following it?
speaking.hintUz: An’anani tasvirlang, keyin “If people stopped …, we would lose …” deb oqibatini ayting.
speaking.textAlternative: Oilangiz yoki viloyatingizdagi bitta an’ana haqida 6 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Who taught you this tradition?
Has it changed over the years?

speaking.questionEn: If you were the mayor of your town, what would you change?
speaking.hintUz: “If I were the mayor, I would …” bilan kamida uçta taklif ayting va sababini tuşuntiring.
speaking.textAlternative: Hokim bölsangiz, şahringizda nimani özgartirardingiz — 6 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: What would you do first?
How would people react?

speaking.questionEn: If you could learn any traditional craft or instrument, which would you choose and why?
speaking.hintUz: “If I could learn …, I would choose … because …” va qayerda örganişingizni ayting.
speaking.textAlternative: Qaysi hunar yoki çolğuni örganardingiz — 5 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: How long would it take to learn?
Who would teach you?

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: colleague — hamkasb.
exercises.question: What does “colleague” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos zamonni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: “Two years ago” — aniq vaqt: Past Simple (moved).
exercises.question: We ___ to Tashkent two years ago.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni Present Perfect şaklida yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: She + has + V3: has achieved.
exercises.text: This year she ___ (achieve) all her goals.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Inkor oxirida yet: I haven’t received it yet.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I didn’t receive my contract yet already.
I haven’t received my contract yet.
I haven’t received my contract already.
I have received not my contract yet.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Heç … ganmisiz?” = Have you ever …? (tajriba).
exercises.source: Siz heç kafeda işlaganmisiz?
accepted: Have you ever worked in a cafe
Have you ever worked in a café
Have you ever worked at a cafe
Have you ever worked at a café

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ega + has + just + V3: She has just sent her CV.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: promotion — lavozimga kötariliş, skill — könikma, hire — işga olmoq, recently — yaqinda.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: “Yesterday” — aniq vaqt; u bilan Present Perfect işlatilmaydi. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: We can say “I have finished the report yesterday.”

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: reliable — işonçli.
exercises.question: What does “reliable” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos modalni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Aniq emas, faqat ehtimol — might.
exercises.question: Take an umbrella. It ___ rain this afternoon.

exercises.instructionUz: Böş joyga must yoki can’t yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Bir soat oldin ovqatlandi — oç bölişi mumkin emas: can’t.
exercises.text: He had a big lunch an hour ago. He ___ be hungry.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Modal + boşlanğiç fe’l: could be.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: It could to be the router.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Uyda bölsa kerak” — dalil bilan taxmin: must be at home.
exercises.source: Chiroq yoniq. U uyda bölsa kerak.
accepted: The light is on. She must be at home
The light is on. He must be at home
The lights are on. She must be at home
The lights are on. He must be at home

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ega + must + be + V-ing: They must be sleeping.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: replace — örnini egallamoq, device — qurilma, improve — yaxşilamoq, probably — ehtimol.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: “Bölişi mumkin emas” taxmini can’t bilan aytiladi, mustn’t bilan emas. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: “It mustn’t be true” means “It is impossible that it is true”.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: souvenir — esdalik sovğasi.
exercises.question: What does “souvenir” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Passive şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Köplik ega + ötgan zamon: were taken.
exercises.question: These photos ___ in Termez last summer.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni Present Simple passive şaklida yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Ega birlik — is + V3: is spoken.
exercises.text: Uzbek ___ (speak) by about 35 million people.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Passive inkor: wasn’t + V3.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Qurilgan” — was built; yil oldidan in.
exercises.source: Bu köprik 1965-yilda qurilgan.
accepted: This bridge was built in 1965
The bridge was built in 1965

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ega + are + V3 + by …: Carpets are made by hand.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: waste — çiqindi, reduce — kamaytirmoq, crowded — odam gavjum, local — mahalliy.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Passive’da bajaruvçi köpinça aytilmaydi; by faqat kerak bölganda qöşiladi. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: In a passive sentence we must always say who did the action with “by”.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: neighbour — qöşni.
exercises.question: What does “neighbour” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Ilgarigi holat: There used to be …
exercises.question: There ___ a park here, but now it’s a car park.

exercises.instructionUz: Böş joyni inkor şaklda töldiring.
exercises.explanationUz: Inkor: didn’t use to + fe’l.
exercises.text: She ___ (not / like) spicy food, but now she loves it.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Holat fe’li (live) bilan would emas, used to: We used to live in Nukus.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: We used to live in Nukus.
We use to live in Nukus.
We were used to live in Nukus.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Ilgari … çekardi” — used to smoke.
exercises.source: Otam ilgari çekardi.
accepted: My father used to smoke
My dad used to smoke

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan söroq gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: Did + ega + use to + fe’l: Did you use to wear glasses?

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: habit — odat, tradition — an’ana, childhood — bolalik, nowadays — hozirgi kunda.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Used to faqat ötmiş uçun. Hozirgi odat — Present Simple. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: We can say “I use to drink tea every morning” about the present.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: ingredient — masalliq.
exercises.question: What does “ingredient” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Natija bölagi — will + fe’l.
exercises.question: If you don’t wash the rice, the plov ___ sticky.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni töğri şaklda yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: When bölagida Present Simple; everyone birlik hisoblanadi: arrives.
exercises.text: We will start eating when everyone ___ (arrive).

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Unless’ning özi inkor: Unless you hurry …
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Unless you don’t hurry, we’ll be late.
Unless you hurry, we’ll be late.
Unless you will hurry, we’ll be late.
Unless you hurry, we are late tomorrow.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “… bilanoq” = as soon as; bölakda Present Simple.
exercises.source: Suv qaynaşi bilanoq guruçni soling.
accepted: Add the rice as soon as the water boils
Put the rice in as soon as the water boils
As soon as the water boils, add the rice
As soon as the water boils add the rice
Put in the rice as soon as the water boils

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: If + Present Simple, … will …: If it rains we will stay home.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: boil — qaynatmoq, fry — qovurmoq, fresh — sarxil, avoid — saqlanmoq.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: If bölagida kelajak ma’nosida ham Present Simple keladi — fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: In “If it rains tomorrow, …” we use the Present Simple, not “will”.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: deadline — oxirgi muddat.
exercises.question: What does “deadline” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Davom etayotgan jarayon + for: have been waiting.
exercises.question: We ___ for the doctor for an hour.

exercises.instructionUz: For yoki since ni yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Monday — boşlaniş nuqtasi: since.
exercises.text: It has been raining ___ Monday.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Miqdor (four emails) — natija: Present Perfect Simple.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I have been sending four emails today.
I have sent four emails today.
I am sending four emails today already.
I have been sent four emails today.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “… dan beri yaşayapsiz” — How long have you been living …?
exercises.source: Toşkentda qançadan beri yaşayapsiz?
accepted: How long have you been living in Tashkent
How long have you lived in Tashkent

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ega + has been + V-ing + for …: She has been working remotely for a year.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: client — mijoz, commute — işga qatnamoq, earn — pul topmoq, lonely — yolğiz.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Know, like, want kabi holat fe’llari continuous’da işlatilmaydi — fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: We don’t usually use “know” in the Present Perfect Continuous.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözning ma’nosini tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: heritage — meros.
exercises.question: What does “heritage” mean?

exercises.instructionUz: Mos şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Xayoliy şart natijasi — would + fe’l.
exercises.question: If I spoke Korean, I ___ in Seoul.

exercises.instructionUz: Fe’lni töğri şaklda yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: If bölagi — Past Simple: had.
exercises.text: If we ___ (have) a garden, we would grow our own vegetables.

exercises.instructionUz: Töğri gapni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: If bölagida would işlatilmaydi.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: If I would be rich, I would help everyone.
If I was rich, I will help everyone.
If I were rich, I would help everyone.
If I am rich, I would help everyone.

exercises.instructionUz: Gapni ingliz tiliga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Men sizning örningizda bölsam” = If I were you.
exercises.source: Men sizning örningizda bölsam, bu gilamni sotmasdim.
accepted: If I were you, I wouldn’t sell this carpet
If I were you, I wouldn't sell this carpet
If I were you, I would not sell this carpet
If I were you I wouldn’t sell this carpet

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlardan gap tuzing.
exercises.explanationUz: ega + would + fe’l + if + Past Simple.

exercises.instructionUz: Sözlarni tarjimasi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: preserve — asramoq, generation — avlod, craft — hunar, proud of — faxrlanmoq.

exercises.instructionUz: Grammatik qoida haqidagi fikr töğrimi (true) yoki xatomi (false)?
exercises.explanationUz: Second Conditional’dagi Past Simple ötgan vaqtni emas, xayoliylikni bildiradi. Fikr xato.
exercises.statement: In “If I had a car, I would drive to work”, the speaker had a car in the past.
